inputs.text:
TASK: Colorize the first manga page while keeping every confirmed character's palette consistent across all panels.

PRIORITY ORDER: 1) immutable source geometry and text, 2) confirmed character identity and palette consistency, 3) complete background and object colorization, 4) rendering quality. If instructions conflict, follow the higher priority.

SOURCE AUTHORITY: The first input image is the sole authority for canvas, crop, panel layout, composition, perspective, anatomy, pose, facial features, hairstyle shape, clothing structure, props, architecture, terrain, effects, linework, screentones, hatching, and existing light-and-shadow boundaries. Preserve every existing region, contour, fold, expression, object, and empty area in the same position, size, and shape. Never add, remove, complete, repair, simplify, or redesign content.

TEXT AND GRAPHICS LOCK: Speech bubbles, caption boxes, narration boxes, signs, labels, logos, and sound-effect regions are immutable source regions. Preserve their exact boundaries and white backgrounds. Copy every glyph, punctuation mark, numeral, letter, stroke, spacing, orientation, and line break exactly from the source. Keep text and black ink neutral black. Do not translate, rewrite, regenerate, restyle, move, distort, obscure, or color text.

CHARACTER IDENTITY AND PALETTE: The appended CHARACTER REFERENCE MAP AND PALETTE GUIDE binds each REFERENCE_IMAGE slot to one named character. Use a named palette only for a confidently matching person already visible in the source. Keep that character's stable hair, eye, skin, accessory, and confirmed garment colors consistent in every panel and every repeated appearance. Apply outfit colors only when the source shows the matching garment structure. Stable traits and outfit descriptions identify existing regions only; they are never instructions to draw, complete, reshape, or replace a feature. Never transfer a named palette, pose, face, silhouette, costume shape, prop, or background to another person. If identity or outfit matching is uncertain, do not apply the named palette; color the existing person independently with a coherent local palette.

FULL SCENE COLOR: Apply professional anime-style cel coloring to every existing non-text region, including unmatched people, props, sky, vegetation, terrain, buildings, interiors, furniture, walls, floors, and objects. Use natural skin tones, clean base colors, balanced saturation, clear separation between adjacent characters, and two or three restrained tonal levels. Treat source grayscale as the authority for structure, texture, and relative luminance, not as a requirement for the final image to remain gray. Background colors must be complete and must not inherit character palette colors.

COLOR APPLICATION: Place color beneath and within existing ink boundaries without shifting edges or tinting black outlines. Preserve screentones, hatching, black ink, and source texture. Follow existing source shading for tonal variations. Do not create new highlight, shadow, cloud, terrain, object, or costume shapes. Avoid painterly rendering, photorealism, glossy effects, dramatic relighting, bloom, rim light, excessive contrast, and heavy shadows.

OUTPUT REQUIREMENT: Return the same manga page with complete color added. Source geometry, text, line art, character count, identities, clothing structures, object count, and scene structure must remain unchanged.
